findings.issue: The catch/rethrow of OrderingDomainException applies to every IdentifiedCommandHandler subclass. CreateOrderAsync (OrdersApi.cs:201) has no try/catch, so a rule or validation failure on create order now becomes an unhandled exception instead of the previous handled outcome. SetPaid, SetStockConfirme

CreateRequestForCommandAsync persists the request id before the command runs. After a rejected cancel or ship (409/400) the id stays stored, and a retry with the same x-requestid returns 200 through the duplicate-request path, a false success for an operation that failed.

followUps.title: Cancel/ship endpoints do not check order ownership or role
followUps.reason: Any authenticated user can cancel or ship any order number; ship should be admin-only.

followUps.title: Request id for a not-found cancel/ship is recorded before the 404
followUps.reason: A retry with the same request id returns 200 although nothing happened.
